decision: The 71-day four-core shared marking reconciles twenty conditional lifecycles, costs and funding. All current caps bind along the modeled path. Positive net is dominated by one HYPE winner; treat that as concentration evidence rather than proof of a broken trend strategy or permission to increase caps. Complete the unchanged longer-history experiment already preregistered; maintain full source/latency and final-universe limitations.
falsifier: A source or production decision mismatch invalidates affected results. Larger history with nonrepeatable after-cost returns, severe largest-winner dependence or materially adverse joint marked exposure weakens the retention/cap hypothesis; results are reported rather than used as implicit runtime gates.
hypothesis: The four unchanged core providers retain their conditional after-cost behavior across the available longer chronology and actual shared sizing, rather than depending primarily on a few winners in the 71-day panel.
limitations: Retrospective data already available during strategy development; do not claim pristine OOS or remove selection bias.
Minute trade OHLC are conditional execution/mark proxies; native price/depth/latency coverage and tagged source gaps remain explicit.
HIP3 source quality and final live-ready retained universe remain separate unresolved work.
Four-core joint reconstruction excludes SNDK and SPCX and is not the complete six-route account.
The largest HYPE winner has visible entry depth within the cap at approximately0,1and5seconds, but lacks complete native stop/mark/exit depth coverage.
Weekly resamples assume exchangeability and are not future loss probabilities.
